description: QoreX is a curious, collaborative team passionate about space, astronomy and useful technology. We enjoy exploring big questions, learning new tools and turning ideas into working solutions. For the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, we aim to make sky observations easier to explore and compare over time. We're looking for teammates skilled in astronomy, Python, AI/ML, web development, data science, UI/UX or research—and, above all, curious, creative people willing to learn and build together.
summary:
We built QoreX, a web-based astronomical workbench that empowers anyone to explore NASA's SPHEREx all-sky infrared survey the way WiseView opened WISE data to citizen science. SPHEREx re-surveys the sky every six months, revealing cool distant worlds, brown dwarfs, and fast-moving stars by blinking between epochs—yet the mission shipped without a public visual discovery tool.

QoreX fills this critical gap. It queries NASA/IPAC IRSA live and reprojects official FITS cutouts onto a common sky grid. Observers can blink, split, difference, and sequence up to eight real exposures on a shared brightness scale, identify sources with proper-motion-propagated Gaia DR3 overlays, and extract 0.75–5μm spectra across 40 exposures in parallel.

Every pixel traces directly to IRSA—nothing is simulated—and reproducible evidence manifests with dataset DOIs export in one click. The tool is verified live across all five challenge targets, including Barnard’s Star with 130 archival records over a 37-day baseline and an automatic 10.4″/yr motion flag
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS —

  • Observational Astronomy Workbench: QoreX is an interactive browser workbench designed for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge that queries official NASA/IPAC IRSA SIA v2 endpoints for real SPHEREx Quick Release (QR3/QR2) observations.
    • B − A Difference Residual: Highlights pixel-level flux changes (Amber = Frame B brighter; Cyan = Frame A brighter).
    • Split View & Sequences: Side-by-side synchronized comparison and 2–8 frame time-series movie playback.
    • Gaia DR3 Astrometric Overlay: Automatically propagates proper motion vectors to the observation epoch, flagging rapid movers like Barnard's Star (10.4″/yr10.4″/\text{yr}10.4″/yr).
    • On-the-Fly Spectrophotometry: Extracts multi-detector aperture photometry across up to 40 exposures in parallel (0.75–5.00 μm0.75–5.00\,\mu\text{m}0.75–5.00μm) with interactive plots and CSV export.

HOW IT WAS BUILD UP (TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES) —

  • Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Astropy (WCS, FITS handling), Reproject (celestial grid alignment), and NumPy.
  • Frontend: Clean, responsive vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript (zero heavy framework overhead).
  • Sky Atlas: Vendored Aladin Lite v3 engine integrated with local NASA/IPAC AllWISE mid-infrared reference cutouts (no CDN reliance).
  • Testing & Verification: 29 automated offline pytest unit tests covering coordinates, bitwise flag masking, and UI contracts, validated against live SPHEREx archive exposures.
  • Deployment: Containerized via Docker; live on AWS EC2 (http://44.239.210.28/) and runnable locally on Windows (run_windows.bat) or Linux/macOS (run_unix.sh).

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED —

  • Science Integrity & Zero Mock Data: QoreX enforces strict scientific honesty. It never fabricates sky images, light curves, or observation timestamps. An empty search result is an explicit state, not filled with placeholders.
  • Bitmask-Aware Flag Masking: Follows the official SPHEREx Explanatory Supplement bit-table (SSDC-DP-017 v2.0) to suppress instrument artifacts while keeping valid astronomical sources visible.
  • Linear Variable Filter (LVF) Geometry: Because adjacent pixels sample different wavelengths, QoreX computes local λ\lambdaλ via the exposure's spectral WCS and provides an explicit wavelength-match verdict for every comparison.
  • Verifiable Provenance: Every rendered frame includes IRSA response header metadata, and sessions can be exported as cryptographic Evidence JSON manifests carrying official dataset DOIs

BENEFITS & IMPACT —

  • Democratizing NASA Data: Bridges the gap between raw mission FITS archives and citizen scientists, students, and professional astronomers worldwide.
  • The Modern Successor to WiseView: Replicates the proven citizen-science discovery paradigm that uncovered hundreds of brown dwarfs and asteroids in WISE data, now unlocked for the SPHEREx era.
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Accessible instantly in any browser with no login, no paywall, and no setup required.
